_note: Structural at-a-glance facts for Delhi's urban water supply, anchored on CAG Report No. 3 of 2025 (tabled 23 Mar 2026; audit period FY2017-18 to 2021-22), the Delhi Economic Survey 2023-24 Ch. 13, and DJB's own water page. Delhi is the platform's second 'pumped-from-far' city after Bengaluru - except nothing is pumped uphill: it arrives by gravity canal from five states, which is why the story stats emphasise distance and instruments, not lift. Source-wise availability figures are DJB's published raw-water splits (Economic Survey); production (~960 MGD = ~4,365 MLD) is the CAG-audited figure - the gap between claimed availability and audited production is itself a finding. Compiled 2026-07-20.

hero_copy.headline: No local storage: piped from five states, one 102-km canal, half the water unbilled
hero_copy.body: Delhi is a fundamentally dependent city. It owns no reservoir: ~90% of its raw water arrives from other states under a stack of instruments - the 1994 five-state Yamuna MoU at Wazirabad, the Munak carrier from Haryana (~70% of the lifeline), Bhakra storage from 240 km away, and Tehri's release riding the Upper Ganga Canal - with its own over-drafted groundwater making up the rest. Nine WTPs turn that into ~960 MGD against a ~1,290+ MGD requirement. What the instruments promise, what the canals deliver, and what the pipes lose on the way is the whole story of Delhi water.
